rows.why: The intended purpose, the types of customers and the settings and laws the customer-facing AI operates in are understood and documented.
Customers are told what the customer-facing AI cannot do and that answers may be wrong, and the limits of its output are documented for the people who oversee it.
The costs to customers and to the business of wrong, harmful or leaked answers reaching customers are examined and documented.
The scope of what the customer-facing AI may answer or do is narrowed and documented, taking public misuse and abuse into account.
The oversight that catches high-impact answers before or after they reach customers is defined, assessed and documented.
Practices and people are in place to take in customer feedback about negative and unexpected impacts and act on it.
Production behaviour of the customer-facing AI is monitored for abuse patterns, unusual answers and high-impact answers, with alerts.
The customer-facing AI is shown to fail safely when pushed beyond its knowledge limits or abused by the public, by declining, handing over to a person or staying within bounds.
Prompt injection and other abuse by public users is tested against the customer-facing AI, and the results are documented and acted on.
Customer interactions and high-impact answers are logged so they can be audited, and overrides and human review of answers are recorded.
Leaks of personal or confidential data in answers to customers are monitored and examined.
Customers can report problems and appeal outcomes, and the reports are counted and fed into evaluation of the application.
Business rules, filters and throttling limit what the customer-facing AI can say or do for the public.
Customer reports of problems and newly found risks are handled through a response and recovery procedure.
The customer-facing AI can be switched off or replaced when answers go wrong, with thresholds and owners defined.
Customer feedback is turned into measurable improvements in each update of the customer-facing AI.
Incidents and errors in front of customers are tracked, communicated to those affected, and reviewed afterwards.

review.reason: LLM-3.14 is about monitoring LLM logs for access to known sensitive data, not leaks in answers shown to customers; it is off-topic for this row (LLM-3.13 DLP on data passing to and from the model fits).
Nothing asks whether post-deployment monitoring of the customer-facing AI is run in practice, including capturing customer input, appeal and override, and change management.
Customer feedback, positive and negative, and how often answers are overridden are not used to check whether the application performs as intended in front of customers.
Nothing checks performance of the customer-facing AI under real public conditions (unexpected, non-optimised use by customers) rather than only lab conditions.
Nothing asks whether the benefits customers are meant to get from the AI are examined, with customer input on perceived benefit, so harms can be weighed against them.
